wells.name: MANNING 13-6 WILDCAT
wells.notes: Well abandoned by cement plugs (Sept. 12-13, 1949): Plug #1 from 4748 to 4675 ft with 50 sacks cement; Plug #2 from 3800 to 3700 ft with 40 sacks cement (felt for and found at 3657 ft); Plug #3 from 3550 to 3450 ft with 42 sacks cement plus 1% calcium chloride; Plug #4 from 2775 to 2700 ft with 30 sacks cement (felt for plug, hit at 3430 ft prior); Run #5 plug from 2650 to 2575 ft with 42 sacks cement (felt for plug #5 at 4 PM, found at 2555 ft); Run #6 plug from 630 to 550 ft with 35 sacks cement, plug felt at 545 ft with 4 points. Operations also included mixing mud, laying down 3 1/2" drill pipe, circulating, waiting on orders, and the rig was released at 4 PM.

wells.name: IMPERIAL FT SASK 7-21
wells.notes:
1953 D&A, Fort Saskatchewan field. Surface casing only to 186.2 m. Tops: Wabamun 1022, Calmar 1053, Nisku 1065, Ireton 1117, Beaverhill Lake 1450 m. 

The well was plugged and abandoned April 10-12, 1953 after reaching total depth (~4801 ft). Seven cement plugs were run: Plug #1, 4801-4751 ft, 25 sax cement, down at 7:20 (Apr 10); Plug #2, 4480-4430 ft, 35 sax cement with 2% C.C., down at 8:30 PM (Apr 10); Plug #3, 3510-3460 ft, 35 sax cement & 2% C.C., down at 7:00, felt O.K. at 3440 (Apr 11); Plug #4, 3100-3050 ft, 35 sax cement and 2% C.C., down at 4:30, felt O.K. with top at 3038 (Apr 11); Plug #5, 2550-2350 ft, 100 sax cement 2% C.C., down at 4:00, felt O.K. at 2345 (Apr 12); Plug #6, 570-640 ft, 40 sax cement with 2% additive, down at 1:30, felt (Apr 12); and Plug #7 set at surface after taking off the B.O.P. (Apr 12). Waiting-on-cement periods were observed between plugs and drill pipe, drill collars and core barrel were laid down at the end of the job.

wells.name: PHOENIX REDWATER 3-17
wells.notes:
1965 D&A, Redwater field. Surface casing only to 185.9 m. Tops: Calmar 1016, Nisku 1029, Ireton 1069, Leduc 1095 m — penetrates caprock and reservoir. Just outside the 5 km circles (~5.1 km from the Pine injector) but inside the review area. 

The well was abandoned with four cement plugs after reaching T.D. 3660' (July 2-4, 1965). Plug No. 1: 3658'-3277' with 170 sx cement, cementing equipment rigged up and plug down @ 5:30 P.M. July 2/65, pulled 15 stands and waited on cement; felt plug No. 1 at 3217'-3219'. Plug No. 2: 3130'-3029' with 50 sx cement and 2% C.C., plug down @ 2:00 A.M., felt at 2994'. Plug No. 3: 2430'-2290' with 64 sx cement and 2% C.C., plug down @ 10:30 A.M., felt at 2275'. Plug No. 4: 660'-560' with 65 sx cement and 2% C.C., plug down @ 8:00 P.M., felt at 520' at 4:00 A.M. Surface casing (8 5/8" 24 lb J-55, 0-610') had been cemented with 320 sx normal cement plus 2% C.C. After the final plug the pipe was laid down, B.O.P. and rig laid down, and the rig was released at 8:00 A.M. July 4/65.

anchors.1: Abandoned to current D020 / Class VI standard; verified plugs across storage complex
anchors.3: Era-standard abandonment; plugs present but unverified (no tag/log)
anchors.5: Improper abandonment; bridge-plug-only / welded-cap era; plugs missing

params.name: Cement Coverage & Quality
params.desc: TOC and cement quality vs. seals and BGWP/USDW base

anchors.1: Returns/CBL confirm coverage across primary seal and to surface-casing shoe
anchors.3: TOC below a required seal, or quality unverified (no CBL/VDL)
anchors.5: Known uncemented interval across a seal or across BGWP/USDW base; no cement records

params.name: Barriers Across Flow Zones
params.desc: Independent permanent barriers per flow zone

anchors.1: ≥2 independent verified barriers per flow zone

params.name: SCVF / Gas Migration History
params.desc: Surface casing vent flow / gas migration test history

anchors.3: Historical SCVF/GM repaired & verified, or never tested

params.name: Well Age & Regulatory Era
params.desc: Drilling year as a proxy for cementing/abandonment practice vintage

params.name: Wellbore Complexity & Condition
params.desc: Deviation, sour/oil service history, casing condition

anchors.3: Deviated, or sour/oil-producer history, or suspected casing issues
anchors.5: Multiple factors, or known casing failure/corrosion

params.name: Penetration vs Storage Complex
params.desc: Deepest penetration relative to primary seal and storage reservoir

params.name: Position vs Plume & Pressure Front
params.desc: Position relative to the modeled CO₂ plume and pressure front (AoR)

anchors.1: Outside modeled pressure front (AoR). No model yet: > 3.2 km from injector
anchors.3: Inside pressure front, outside plume. No model yet: 1.6 – 3.2 km
anchors.5: Inside modeled CO₂ plume extent. No model yet: < 1.6 km

params.name: Groundwater (USDW/BGWP) Isolation
params.desc: Barrier status across the protected groundwater interval

anchors.1: Verified isolation across BGWP/USDW base (surface casing + cement, or plugs)
anchors.5: Known open pathway at the groundwater interval

params.name: Corrective-Action Accessibility
params.desc: Feasibility of re-entry / re-abandonment if intervention is needed

anchors.1: Licensee active; surface access; re-entry feasible
anchors.5: Orphaned, unknown location, or re-entry infeasible

Type 1.desc: No documentation available, minimal or no records; only drilling is known. Construction details are absent, so schematics cannot be produced.

Type 2.desc: Penetrates both the primary geologic seal and storage reservoir.
Type 2.prot: No protection for groundwater/USDWs, primary geologic seal, or storage reservoir.

Type 3.desc: Penetrates both the primary geologic seal and storage reservoir.
Type 3.prot: Protection for groundwater/USDWs only; no protection for primary geologic seal or storage reservoir.

Type 4.desc: Penetrates both the primary geologic seal and storage reservoir.
Type 4.prot: Protection for groundwater/USDWs and primary geologic seal; storage reservoir not protected.

Type 5.desc: Penetrates only the primary geologic seal.
Type 5.prot: No protection for groundwater/USDWs or primary geologic seal.

Type 6.desc: Penetrates only the primary geologic seal.
Type 6.prot: Protection for groundwater/USDWs; primary geologic seal not protected.

Type 7.desc: Penetrates both the primary geologic seal and storage reservoir.
Type 7.prot: Protection for groundwater/USDWs, primary geologic seal, and storage reservoir.

Type 8.desc: Penetrates only the primary geologic seal.
Type 8.prot: Protection for groundwater/USDWs and primary geologic seal.

Type 9.desc: Does not penetrate either the primary geologic seal or storage reservoir.
Type 9.prot: Dependent on confining-zone integrity; if the confining zone is intact, represents the lowest level of risk.
